appraisal_events.evidence: « Parisien dont l'esprit était apprécié de tous, comme la sûreté de ses relations choisies mais fidèles, il sera unanimement regretté [...] au Jockey-Club dont il était l'un des membres les plus anciens et les plus écoutés. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The quoted Gaulois obituary praises Swann's taste, refined connections, and standing at the Jockey-Club, presenting him as esteemed and mourned by fashionable society.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Swann était, au contraire, une remarquable personnalité intellectuelle et artistique [...] c'est parce que celui que vous deviez considérer comme un petit imbécile a fait de vous le héros d'un de ses romans [...] que peut-être vous vivrez. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Unlike the ephemeral bourgeois names the narrator contrasts him with, Swann is affirmed as a genuinely distinguished figure and granted a form of survival through being made the hero of the narrator's novel, an endorsed and self-referential elevation.

status_effects.explanation: Both the obituary's praise and the narrator's endorsed commentary present Swann as a distinguished figure whose memory and reputation persist beyond his death.
The obituary underscores his long-standing, respected membership in fashionable clubs, marking recognized social prestige, though the surrounding meditation notes such fame is ultimately fragile.
